record.paper_title: Concrete examples of the rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations: numerical results for the heat semigroup and open questions on them (with appendix: full list of pictures and Python code)
record.original_question: Let UC_b(R,R) be the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions on R with the sup norm. Given arbitrary a,b,c in UC_b(R,R) with a(x) bounded below by a positive constant, let L be the second-order variable-coefficient differential operator (Lf)(x)=a(x)f''(x)+b(x)f'(x)+c(x)f(x) on C_b^∞(R,R), whose closure generates a C_0-semigroup e^{tL}. Does there exist an explicitly computable family C(t) of bounded linear operators on UC_b(R,R), expressed directly in terms of a,b,c,f,x and not using e^{tL} even implicitly, such that C is a Chernoff function for L and, on some dense subspace D, the approximation error satisfies ||e^{tL}f-C(t/n)^n f|| ≤ M/q^n for constants M>0 and q>1 for all sufficiently large n? If such superfast Chernoff approximations do not exist, what obstruction proves their impossibility?

evidence.quote: In the List of open problems in the One-parameter semigroups theory [13] there is the following problem:Provide a concrete example of a super-fast (at least exponentially) converging Chernoff approximation to a semigroup generated by a first-order differential operator with variable coefficients, with Chernoff function explicitly expressed in terms of these coefficients and without circulus vitiosus of any kind, e.g. in the form of using the values of the semigroup for creating a Chernoff function for it.
The open problemis to find a family (C(t))t≥0 of linear bounded operators defined everywhere inU C b(R,R) which has the following three properties:
There exists a dense linear subspaceDinU C b(R,R) and constantsM >0, q >1, n 0 >0 such that ∥etLf−C(t/n) nf∥ ≤M/q n for alln≥n 0 and allf∈D;

Cis defined by an explicitly given formula (C(t)f)(x) =F(a, b, c, f, x) and the calculation ofe tL is not included into this formula, even in a hidden way, so expression etL = lim n→∞ C(t/n) n is free from circulus vitiosus of any kind and can be used as a practical method of calculation ofe tL.

Effective methods for constructing superfast converging Chernoff approximations for this operatorLare not known at present. However, there are no fundamental objections to their existence either, which presents a challenge to either find such approximations or to prove that they are impossible for some reason.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ denote the Banach space of bounded uniformly continuous real-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$, equipped with the supremum norm $\|\cdot\|$. Fix functions $a,b,c \in UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ with $\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}} a(x) > 0$. On the domain $C_b^\infty(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ of bounded smooth functions with bounded derivatives of all orders, define the second-order variable-coefficient differential operator
\[ (Lf)(x) = a(x)f''(x) + b(x)f'(x) + c(x)f(x). \]
Assume that the closure of $L$ generates a strongly continuous semigroup $(e^{tL})_{t\ge 0}$ on $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$.

Recall that a family $(C(t))_{t\ge 0}$ of bounded linear operators on $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ is called a Chernoff function for $L$ if $C(0)=I$, $\sup_{t\in[0,T]}\|C(t)\|<\infty$ for every $T>0$, $C(t)f$ is continuous in $t$ for every $f$, and $\lim_{t\to 0^+}(C(t)f-f)/t = Lf$ for $f$ in a core of $L$; in this case Chernoff's theorem yields $e^{tL}f = \lim_{n\to\infty} C(t/n)^n f$.

Question. Do there exist a family $(C(t))_{t\ge 0}$ of bounded linear operators on $UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ and a dense linear subspace $D \subset UC_b(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R})$ such that:

(i) $(C(t))_{t\ge 0}$ is a Chernoff function for $L$;

(ii) there is an explicit formula $(C(t)f)(x) = F(a,b,c,f,x;t)$ depending only on the coefficients $a,b,c$, on $f$, and on $x,t$, and in particular not involving the semigroup $e^{tL}$ (neither explicitly nor in any hidden way);

(iii) there exist constants $M>0$, $q>1$, and $n_0\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $f\in D$ and every $t$ in a fixed bounded interval,
\[ \|e^{tL}f - C(t/n)^n f\| \le \frac{M}{q^n} \quad \text{for all } n \ge n_0? \]

If no such "superfast" Chernoff approximation exists, exhibit an obstruction proving its impossibility.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears on a published list of open problems in one-parameter semigroup theory and is reiterated in recent works (2023) on Chernoff approximations. Known fast-converging Chernoff approximations either rely on the semigroup itself (circulus vitiosus) or are restricted to constant-coefficient/model examples (heat and transport equations); no explicit superfast Chernoff function for general variable coefficients has been exhibited, and no impossibility result is known. The status is open.

status_evidence.title: Chernoff approximations as a method for finding the resolvent... (arXiv:2301.06765)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Chernoff approximations for operators with variable coefficients and references the open-problem list in one-parameter semigroup theory.
status_evidence.claim: The superfast variable-coefficient Chernoff approximation problem is referenced as an open question in recent literature.

status_evidence.title: Speed of convergence of Chernoff approximations for two model examples
status_evidence.snippet: Studies rate of convergence of Chernoff approximations only for heat and transport equation model examples.
status_evidence.claim: Existing results on fast-convergence of Chernoff approximations are limited to model constant-coefficient examples.

status_evidence.title: Upper and lower estimates for rate of convergence in the Chernoff product formula
status_evidence.snippet: Provides general upper and lower bounds for convergence rates in Chernoff's product formula, without resolving the variable-coefficient superfast case.
status_evidence.claim: General bounds exist but the specific superfast variable-coefficient problem remains unresolved.
